messages:
emily: FYI on a support escalation — multiple NA customers reporting SSE streams that stop sending new 'data:' frames for ~30-90s then resume. Happens across hosted endpoints.
emily: Not full disconnects (conn stays open), just long silent gaps then a burst of tokens. Customers see partial outputs and duplicate resumes.
support-lead: Received 12 tickets in last hour, highest priority customer affected. Asking for mitigation steps + status update to customers.
aj: Seeing same in our telemetry — spike in stream idle durations starting ~2033999800, primarily us-east-1 fanout nodes. Error rates roughly flat, but per-connection last_event_ts shows pauses.
aj: Dumping a single example connection: 
```
client_id=acct-12
conn_id=conn-9f3a
last_event_ts=2033999958
next_chunk_ts=2034000032
frames_sent=312
frames_received=0
```
aj: Not seeing TCP resets or HTTP 5xx, so likely server-side stall in the fanout loop.
mike: Can you repro with curl? I want a deterministic trace.
emily: Repro steps support gave: 
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-large&prompt=hello&stream=true"
# observe 'data:' frames, then silence ~45s, then resume
```
emily: Support logs show client keepalive pings still received during silence. So connection alive.
sre-bot: Alert created: SEV2 - NA SSE degradation. Linked runbook: sse-fanout-degrade-v2.
aj: Short-term mitigation idea: route affected traffic to hot fallback pool in na-west that uses the dedicated fanout (lower fanout concurrency) until fix. Requires routing change + TTL update.
mike: Also trigger a soft rollback of the last runtime micro-optim that touched the streaming write loop (deployed ~2033999600). I suspect a change to the batching loop introduced intermittent backpressure stalls.
emily: Agreed. We're seeing correlation with that deploy. Can ops rollback?
ops-rotation: Rolling back runtime micro-optim now. ETA ~6m. I'll also add a temporary retry policy on client library: increase client-side keepalive frequency + server-side streaming flush every 1s for affected pool.
support-lead: I'll send a customer-facing status: we have identified a streaming write stall introduced in a recent runtime change. Mitigating by rollback and routing to fallback pools. Next update in 30m.
aj: After rollback started: metric for stream idle percent dropped from 12% -> 2% over 4m on rollback nodes. Routing change in progress to shift 20% -> 0% for affected nodes.
emily: For engineering postmortem: need repro harness that simulates heavy fanout with long-lived streams and KV-cache churn. Also add an active monitor that fails if last_event_age > 10s for >1% of connections.
mike: Billing note: some customers saw duplicate resumed chunks and were charged for tokens that later deduped in client. We'll need to coordinate with finance on credits for impacted windows.
support-lead: Posted interim status on status.redwood.ai and replied to top 5 customers with ETA and credits promise.
aj: Follow-up: pushed a small server-side flush change to affected pool (force flush on write loop every 800ms) as additional mitigation while rollback completes. Observed immediate reduction in silent gaps for canary.
ops-rotation: Rollback finished. Routing moved back after 12m. All primary metrics normalizing.
emily: Closing loop: capture snapshot of traces for the incident window, create postmortem, and add regression test in CI. I'll assign owners.
support-lead: Thanks team — customers updated, credits queued. I'll keep incident open for postmortem until owners file docs.
